findings.statement: A historical FrankEye implementation explicitly integrated a saved Digital Retina v8 CNN classifier with HOG/color features, DINOv2 scene features, GOLPU-derived visual features, Tesseract OCR and OpenCV face detection into one CPU-oriented perception pipeline.

The earlier module named frank_adaptive_vision implemented adaptive computation/routing, not online user-specific visual learning: it ran a fast detector pipeline and escalated low-confidence or semantically demanding cases to a local VLM.
Commit 0fd27f23 removed frank_adaptive_vision.py and frank_visual_pipeline.py while consolidating vision into FrankEye.

The frozen-head tools/native_vision.py replaces FrankEye with a direct Qwen3.5-4B multimodal llama-server bridge and explicitly states that CNN, DINOv2, ONNX and Tesseract are no longer used in that bridge.

Within the reviewed frozen-head native_vision.py implementation, no persistent user-specific classifier/prototype memory, trusted-example lineage, online familiarity update, open-set calibration, candidate promotion, rollback or cyclic learner state is implemented. Native multimodal inference therefore does not by itself demonstrate the Clay 0.1 adaptive visual-learning contract.

lineage: -> unified engineered perception with Digital Retina v8 inheritance (FrankEye)
-> direct foundation-model multimodal perception bridge (native_vision at frozen head)

architecture_implications.statement: Clay 0.1 should distinguish perceptual description from learned familiarity. Native multimodal Qwen output may supply semantic observations, but personal known/unknown/familiarity state requires an explicit learner with provenance, confidence/open-set behavior and rollback semantics.

Historical Digital Retina/FrankEye mechanisms are reusable primarily as a measurement/feature/latency foundation. The old CIFAR-oriented classifier is not equivalent to the required user-specific Micro Visual Classifier and should not be promoted as such without a discriminating test.

A low-cost integration hypothesis is to keep native Qwen multimodal perception as semantic perception while attaching a bounded personal micro-classifier/prototype learner to a stable visual feature surface, with explicit version identity, trusted-example tiers, calibration, promotion and rollback. The feature source remains an empirical choice and must be benchmarked rather than assumed.

negative_results_preserved: The historical name 'adaptive vision' must not be interpreted as evidence of online user-specific visual learning; the inspected implementation adapts escalation decisions only.
The frozen-head native vision bridge contains no inspected evidence of the required personal cyclic visual learner state.

earned_work_mapping.reason: Row-level mechanism overlap with existing Retina/Drive mappings is not yet reconciled; no duplicate historical-work credit is awarded.

branch_feedback.frank: Preserve native multimodal perception but do not conflate it with personal learned familiarity.
branch_feedback.harness: H1/H2/H3 tests need separate receipts for sensor observation versus user-specific familiarity/classifier state transitions.
branch_feedback.claycode: ClayCode must be able to represent classifier/prototype version, trusted training-example provenance, confidence/open-set result, promotion/rollback and replay/budget semantics if the current adaptive visual-learning directive is retained.
branch_feedback.claygraph: Visual evidence nodes and learned familiarity/prototype nodes should retain provenance and version links rather than collapsing sensor truth into learned identity.
branch_feedback.unifieddb: Persist feature-backbone compatibility, classifier/prototype version identity, trusted-example lineage, calibration metadata and rollback/rebuild state separately from raw/native vision observations.

falsifiers_and_next_tests: Search additional Project-Frankenstein history and Drive Retina artifacts for a distinct online personal visual learner that predates or survives the reviewed files; if found, PF-VIS-005 must be narrowed or superseded.
Benchmark candidate stable visual feature surfaces for same-object/user-specific familiarity under lighting/viewpoint/OOD shifts before selecting the Micro Visual Classifier substrate.

Differentially replay identical image streams through native perception alone versus native perception plus bounded personal learner to quantify added familiarity accuracy, false-known rate, latency, memory cost and rollback fidelity.
